q: In session-setting merge code, how can a per-request mapping remove a key inherited from the session?
anchor:
# Remove keys that are set to None. Extract keys first to avoid altering
    # the dictionary during iteration.
    none_keys = [k for (k, v) in merged_setting.items() if v is None]
    for key in none_keys:
        del merged_setting[key]
fact: Mapping entries whose merged value is None are deleted.

q: Find the redirect implementation that drops credentials when the destination host changes.
anchor:
if old_parsed.hostname != new_parsed.hostname:
            return True
fact: A changed hostname makes should_strip_auth return True.

q: Does the authentication-stripping decision permit an ordinary same-host upgrade from unencrypted to encrypted transport?
anchor:
# Special case: allow http -> https redirect when using the standard
        # ports.
fact: A same-host HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect on standard ports is allowed without stripping authentication.

q: Which three payload headers does redirect resolution remove when the response is neither temporary nor permanent redirect?
anchor:
purged_headers = ("Content-Length", "Content-Type", "Transfer-Encoding")
                for header in purged_headers:
                    prepared_request.headers.pop(header, None)
                prepared_request.body = None
fact: Those redirects clear Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding, and the body.

q: When two connection adapters match a destination prefix, what ordering does the session registration code maintain?
anchor: Adapters are sorted in descending order by prefix length.
fact: Adapter prefixes are sorted longest first.

q: Where does request URL preparation discard leading whitespace before parsing the address?
anchor:
# Remove leading whitespaces from url
        url = url.lstrip()
fact: URL preparation strips leading whitespace.

q: In the request model implementation, what error is built for a web address lacking a scheme?
fact: A missing URL scheme raises MissingSchema with a suggestion to use HTTPS.

q: Find the body-preparation branch that refuses nonfinite numbers while serializing a JSON payload.
fact: JSON serialization disables NaN and translates a ValueError into InvalidJSONError.

q: Which response iterator implementation lets a streaming download avoid loading its whole body into memory?
anchor:
When stream=True is set on the
        request, this avoids reading the content at once into memory for
        large responses.
fact: iter_content avoids reading an entire large response into memory when streaming is enabled.

q: In response error construction, how are client failures distinguished from server failures by status range?
fact: Statuses 400 through 499 produce Client Error messages; 500 through 599 produce Server Error messages.

q: Find the URI utility whose decoding preserves reserved characters and non-ASCII bytes in escaped form.
anchor:
Un-escape any percent-escape sequences in a URI that are unreserved
    characters. This leaves all reserved, illegal and non-ASCII bytes encoded.
fact: unquote_unreserved decodes only unreserved characters.

q: What does the incremental response decoder yield when no encoding has been selected?
fact: Without an encoding it passes the iterator chunks through unchanged.

q: When both a host-specific proxy and a generic scheme proxy are configured, which key order does the proxy selector try?
anchor:
proxy_keys = [
        urlparts.scheme + "://" + urlparts.hostname,
        urlparts.scheme,
        "all://" + urlparts.hostname,
        "all",
    ]
fact: Proxy selection tries scheme-plus-host, scheme, all-plus-host, then all.

q: How does JSON encoding detection account for a UTF-8 byte-order marker?
anchor:
if sample[:3] == codecs.BOM_UTF8:
        return "utf-8-sig"
fact: A UTF-8 BOM selects utf-8-sig.

q: Locate the redirect helper that restores a request-body stream to its recorded initial position and reports an unrewindable stream.
fact: rewind_body seeks to the recorded integer body position when a seek method is available.

q: In the choice-conversion implementation, is the returned value the normalized spelling or one of the original choices?
anchor:
The resulting value will always be one of the originally passed choices
    regardless of ``case_sensitive`` or any ``ctx.token_normalize_func``
    being specified.
fact: The returned value is an originally supplied choice even when normalization or case folding is used.

q: How does the date parameter converter choose among several accepted date formats?
anchor:
Parsing is tried using each format, in order, and the first format which
    parses successfully is used.
fact: DateTime accepts the first successfully parsed format in the configured order.

q: What does integer range conversion do to an out-of-bounds value when clamping is enabled?
anchor:
If ``clamp`` is enabled, a value outside the range is clamped to the
    boundary instead of failing.

    .. versionchanged:: 8.0
fact: Clamping changes an out-of-range integer to a valid boundary instead of failing.

q: Why does constructing a floating-point range with an open endpoint and clamping fail in the type implementation?
anchor:
if (min_open or max_open) and clamp:
            raise TypeError("Clamping is not supported for open bounds.")
fact: An open floating-point boundary combined with clamping raises TypeError.

q: Which file parameter-type behavior stages output beside the original file and replaces it on completion?
anchor:
Starting with Click 2.0, files can also be opened atomically in which
    case all writes go into a separate file in the same folder and upon
    completion the file will be moved over to the original location.
fact: Atomic file mode writes to a separate file in the same folder and moves it over the original on completion.

q: A password-setup flow should ask the user to repeat the entered value; which prompt behavior supports that?
anchor:
:param confirmation_prompt: Prompt a second time to confirm the
        value. Can be set to a string instead of ``True`` to customize
        the message.
fact: confirmation_prompt requests a second entry and can use a custom confirmation message.

q: What exception does the confirmation helper raise after a negative response when aborting was requested?
anchor:
if abort and not rv:
        raise Abort()
fact: A negative confirmation with abort enabled raises Abort.

q: Why can progress output disappear when a command is piped to another process?
anchor:
By default, this progress bar
    will not be rendered if the file is not a terminal.
fact: The progress bar is not rendered by default on non-terminal output.

q: Which editor option makes an unsaved edit return no replacement text?
anchor:
:param require_save: if this is true, then not saving in the editor
                         will make the return value become `None`.
fact: require_save=True causes an unsaved edit to return None.

q: Find the pause implementation that avoids waiting for a keystroke when either input or output is redirected.
anchor:
if not isatty(sys.stdin) or not isatty(sys.stdout):
        return
fact: pause returns immediately unless both standard input and standard output are terminals.

q: In the low-level option parser, what token ends option processing even when custom prefixes exist?
anchor:
# Double dashes always handled explicitly regardless of what
            # prefixes are valid.
            if arg == "--":
                return
fact: A standalone double dash always ends option processing.

q: What happens to the first positional token when interspersed options are disabled in the parser?
fact: With interspersed options disabled the positional token is put back and option scanning stops.

q: Does the long-option matcher silently accept an unregistered abbreviated option name?
anchor:
if opt not in self._long_opt:
            from difflib import get_close_matches

            possibilities = get_close_matches(opt, self._long_opt)
            raise NoSuchOption(opt, possibilities=possibilities, ctx=self.ctx)
fact: An unregistered long option raises NoSuchOption, with close-match suggestions rather than silent acceptance.

q: How does a short option that consumes a value handle characters attached after it in the same token?
fact: Remaining characters are inserted as the value input and grouped short-option scanning stops.

q: Which parser action increments its existing stored value instead of overwriting it?
anchor:
elif self.action == "count":
            state.opts[self.dest] = state.opts.get(self.dest, 0) + 1
fact: The count action increments the destination value, starting at zero.

q: In the Requests quickstart, why might one key in a query-parameter dictionary be absent from the final URL?
anchor:
Note that any dictionary key whose value is ``None`` will not be added to the
URL's query string.
fact: Query-string entries whose dictionary value is None are omitted.

q: A server returned a parseable JSON error document. What does the quickstart recommend checking before calling the request successful?
anchor:
It should be noted that the success of the call to ``r.json()`` does **not**
indicate the success of the response. Some servers may return a JSON object in a
failed response (e.g. error details with HTTP 500). Such JSON will be decoded
and returned. To check that a request is successful, use
``r.raise_for_status()`` or check ``r.status_code`` is what you expect.
fact: Successful JSON decoding does not establish HTTP success; check raise_for_status or the expected status_code.

q: Which payload argument loses precedence if a caller supplies form data or uploaded files as well?
anchor: Note, the ``json`` parameter is ignored if either ``data`` or ``files`` is passed.
fact: The json parameter is ignored when data or files is supplied.

q: How is the redirect response history ordered in the introductory Requests guide?
anchor:
The :attr:`Response.history <requests.Response.history>` list contains the
:class:`Response <requests.Response>` objects that were created in order to
complete the request. The list is sorted from the oldest to the most recent
response.
fact: Response.history is ordered from the oldest redirect response to the most recent.

q: Why is a five-second Requests timeout not necessarily a five-second cap on downloading the complete response?
fact: The timeout concerns a period without a response/socket data, not a total-download deadline.

q: I repeatedly call the same host and want both cookies and established connections reused. Which documented Requests object provides that?
anchor:
The Session object allows you to persist certain parameters across
requests. It also persists cookies across all requests made from the
Session instance, and will use ``urllib3``'s `connection pooling`_.
fact: A Session persists cookies and uses connection pooling across its requests.

q: How should a manually customized prepared request be built so that session cookies are still applied?
anchor:
:class:`Session <requests.Session>`-level state such as cookies will
not get applied to your request. To get a
:class:`PreparedRequest <requests.PreparedRequest>` with that state
applied, replace the call to :meth:`Request.prepare()
<requests.Request.prepare>` with a call to
:meth:`Session.prepare_request() <requests.Session.prepare_request>`
fact: Use Session.prepare_request rather than Request.prepare to apply session state.

q: A streamed response was only partly consumed. What must happen before its connection can return to the pool?
anchor:
If you set ``stream`` to ``True`` when making a request, Requests cannot
release the connection back to the pool unless you consume all the data or call
:meth:`Response.close <requests.Response.close>`.
fact: Consume all response data or explicitly close the response before its connection is released.

q: Where is the usage pattern for setting connection establishment and response-read waiting limits separately?
anchor:
The timeout value will be applied to both the ``connect`` and the ``read``
timeouts. Specify a tuple if you would like to set the values separately::

    r = requests.get('https://github.com', timeout=(3.05, 27))
fact: A two-element timeout tuple sets connect and read timeouts separately.

q: Why may connecting to a hostname with several unreachable addresses take longer than the configured connection timeout?
anchor:
The connect timeout applies to each connection attempt to an IP address.
          If multiple addresses exist for a domain name, the underlying ``urllib3`` will
          try each address sequentially until one successfully connects.
fact: The connect timeout applies to each IP-address attempt and addresses are tried sequentially.

q: What concise credentials representation does the authentication guide show as equivalent to constructing a Basic Auth handler?
anchor:
Providing the credentials in a tuple like this is exactly the same as the
``HTTPBasicAuth`` example above.
fact: A username/password tuple is equivalent to the HTTPBasicAuth example.

q: When no explicit authentication handler is supplied, what credential source can override a manually supplied authorization header?
anchor:
If no authentication method is given with the ``auth`` argument, Requests will
attempt to get the authentication credentials for the URL's hostname from the
user's netrc file. The netrc file overrides raw HTTP authentication headers
set with `headers=`.
fact: Requests can use hostname credentials from netrc, which override raw authentication headers.

q: Where does the Requests authentication guide demonstrate its built-in challenge-response digest handler?
anchor:
from requests.auth import HTTPDigestAuth
    >>> url = 'https://httpbin.org/digest-auth/auth/user/pass'
    >>> requests.get(url, auth=HTTPDigestAuth('user', 'pass'))
fact: HTTPDigestAuth is the built-in digest authentication handler shown by the guide.

q: Which add-on does the Requests guide name for OAuth 2 flows and the mechanism underlying OpenID Connect?
anchor:
The ``requests-oauthlib`` library also handles OAuth 2, the authentication mechanism
underpinning OpenID Connect.
fact: requests-oauthlib handles OAuth 2 and its OpenID Connect foundation.

q: I need a custom authentication scheme. What extension point must my handler subclass and implement?
anchor:
To do so, subclass :class:`AuthBase <requests.auth.AuthBase>` and implement the
``__call__()`` method
fact: Subclass AuthBase and implement __call__ to add custom authentication.

q: For a positional command parameter with neither a declared type nor a default, which type does the argument guide choose?
anchor:
If no
type is provided, the type of the default value is used, and if no default
value is provided, the type is assumed to be :data:`STRING`.
fact: Without an explicit type or default, the positional argument type is STRING.

q: How can a command accept an unbounded set of positional inputs, and how many such variadic parameters may it define?
anchor:
the ``nargs`` parameter.  If it is set to ``-1``, then an unlimited number
of arguments is accepted.

The value is then passed as a tuple.  Note that only one argument can be
set to ``nargs=-1``, as it will eat up all arguments.
fact: nargs=-1 accepts unlimited positional values as a tuple and only one argument may use it.

q: I only need to validate that a supplied filename exists, without opening the file. Which argument type does the tutorial recommend?
anchor:
The :class:`Path` type has several checks available which raise nice
errors if they fail, such as existence.
fact: The Path type can validate a filename, including existence, without opening it.

q: Can positional arguments automatically derive environment-variable names from a common prefix?
anchor:
Unlike options, however, this is only supported for explicitly named
environment variables.
fact: Arguments support explicitly named environment variables rather than automatic prefix-based names.

q: A legitimate input filename begins with a dash. How can the caller keep the argument parser from treating it as an option?
anchor:
accept the string ``--`` as a separator for options and
arguments.  After the ``--`` marker, all further parameters are accepted as
arguments.
fact: Put a standalone -- before option-like filenames to treat subsequent tokens as arguments.

q: I need a single option to accept a name and a numeric identifier of different types. How should its type be declared?
anchor:
By using a tuple literal as type, `nargs` gets automatically set to the
length of the tuple and the :class:`click.Tuple` type is automatically
used.
fact: A tuple literal type supplies heterogeneous component types and automatically sets nargs.

q: How should a default be represented for an option that can be repeated, so it is not split into individual characters?
anchor:
When passing a ``default`` with ``multiple=True``, the default value
must be a list or tuple, otherwise it will be interpreted as a list of
single characters.
fact: Use a list or tuple default for multiple=True.

q: Which option setting supports a verbosity level that rises each time the flag is repeated?
anchor:
use the repetition
of options to count an integer up.
fact: A counting option increments an integer for repeated occurrences.

q: A user-configurable default should still permit an interactive prompt. What approach is recommended instead of a default map?
anchor:
If you want to let the user configure the default value, but still be
prompted if the option isn't specified on the command line, you can do so
by supplying a callable as the default value.
fact: Supply a callable default so the prompt can still occur when no command-line value is given.

q: When a repeated path option reads values from the environment, what separators does the option guide use on Unix and Windows?
anchor:
The default implementation for all types is to split on whitespace.  The
exceptions to this rule are the :class:`File` and :class:`Path` types
which both split according to the operating system's path splitting rules.
On Unix systems like Linux and OS X, the splitting happens for those on
every colon (``:``), and for Windows, on every semicolon (``;``).
fact: File and Path environment values use colons on Unix and semicolons on Windows.

q: When an inner subcommand runs, what happens to the enclosing command-group callback by default?
anchor:
the callback fires whenever a subcommand fires (unless this behavior is
changed).  What this means in practice is that an outer command runs
when an inner command runs
fact: A group callback runs when one of its subcommands runs.

q: Where must options belonging to a particular command be placed relative to that command and its subcommands?
anchor:
options and arguments for a specific command have to be specified
*after* the command name itself, but *before* any other command names.
fact: Command parameters belong after that command name and before subsequent command names.

q: How can a command group execute its callback even when the user has supplied no subcommand?
anchor:
``invoke_without_command=True`` to a group.  In that case, the callback is
always invoked instead of showing the help page.
fact: Set invoke_without_command=True to run the group callback without a subcommand.

q: Which positional argument in a chained-command interface is allowed to consume an unlimited number of values?
anchor:
When using multi command chaining you can only have one command (the last)
use ``nargs=-1`` on an argument.
fact: Only the final command in a chain may have an nargs=-1 argument.

q: Why does the pipeline tutorial advise opening an input file manually rather than retaining a file parameter for later processor functions?
anchor:
Click shuts down the context after
each callback has been run.  This means that for instance file types
cannot be accessed in the `processor` functions as the files will already
be closed there.
fact: Callback contexts close their file parameters before later processor functions run.
